chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ẓarīf, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

For the ḥārisah, which is like a scratch, there is one camel; for the dāmiyah, two camels; for the bāḍiʿah, which is less than the simḥāq, three camels; for the simḥāq, which is less than the mūḍiḥah, four camels; and for the mūḍiḥah, five camels.

key_terms.الدَّامِيَةِ: a wound that draws blood, with a specified compensation
key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a wound reaching the thin membrane before the bone, with four camels as compensation
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit used here for legal blood-compensation
key_terms.الْبَاضِعَةِ: a deeper wound below the level of al-simḥāq, carrying three camels as diyah
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone, with five camels as diyah
key_terms.بَعِيرَانِ: two camels, the compensation amount for al-dāmiyah

ai.seo_question: What are the diyah amounts for different kinds of head wounds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed diyah amounts for several graded types of head or facial wounds. It reflects a structured legal classification in fiqh for bodily injuries, assigning compensation according to the severity of the wound.
